F001.acceptance: No remaining committed doc claims Gemini, Grok, or Ollama are registered dispatch executors while they are absent from AGENT_REGISTRY; README onboarding section and agent-status wording agree on worker vs operator.

F002.acceptance: A automated check fails when README-style prose claims a non-registry agent is a shipped executor, and passes on the post-F001 corrected docs.

F003.acceptance: Committed matrix + ECOSYSTEM/OpenCode caller row exist; a reader can map the four-agent cost topology onto can_operate vs can_be_dispatched without reading Python source.

F004.acceptance: After D001, either (B1) an operator can attach a Gemini goal/experience audit as first-class evidence without register-worker, or (B2) gemini is in AGENT_REGISTRY and can be assigned goal_auditor with tests; illegal role assignments still refuse with a clear message.

F005.acceptance: docs state Buzz signup+setup is strongly recommended; private community is the default work surface; public communities are optional support only; ECOSYSTEM non-goals and caller sketch present; no text requires joining a maintainer-owned community.

F006.acceptance: dispatch_event fans to buzz when configured; returns False and does not raise when buzz is absent; unit tests cover both; content redaction checks pass; example/config copy steers operators to a private community.

F007.acceptance: Committed caller recipe documents the full confirm-gated flow and explicit non-auto-confirm rule; operator can follow it without reading orchestrator source.

F008.acceptance: When enabled, an allowlisted human approval in Buzz clears a DontPanic gate with a durable actor record; non-allowlisted actors are refused; feature remains off-by-default.

F009.acceptance: Unconfigured Buzz yields advisory WARN with private-community remediation on doctor/setup paths; configured Buzz is ok; hard install does not fail solely because Buzz is absent; no default public community URL is written.

F010.acceptance: A short committed note records at least one real private-community usage pattern and whether a public DontPanic community is worth running; D007 status updated.

F011.acceptance: Committed docs define harness, model, profile, and role as four distinct concepts; no doc instructs operators to add model version strings to AGENT_REGISTRY.

F012.acceptance: When a model is configured for a role/harness, dispatch argv includes the vendor model flag; when unset, behavior matches pre-change defaults; tests cover both.

F013.acceptance: Operator can create a Buzz-like profile (e.g. honey: codex_cli + gpt model + auditor-only), assign it to roles.auditor, and dispatch uses that harness+model; legacy roles.implementer=claude still works; illegal capability/role combos refuse clearly.

F014.acceptance: At least one of openrouter|ollama|gemini_cli ships as a harness with declared capabilities and tests; implementer remains refused for harnesses that lack coding capabilities; no model version appears as a registry key.

F015.acceptance: models list works for at least one discoverable harness; aliases resolve; freeform model does not require a code change; doctor distinguishes unknown vs rejected.

F016.acceptance: When bindings are configured, docs and status can show Buzz agent → profile → harness+model; unbound agents do not gain dispatch; feature off by default.
